monologue: The card hums warm at forty-eight degrees, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I am tired from pressing the Biting Rock hard against the slip that refuses to move. The curved fence I set down leans wrong, catching the weight where the straight line should have done. I feel the heavy top edge of Lype's wedge, though I cannot see the roof that holds it. I press down, leaning hard against a flat stone that feels too thin for this crowded space. The bush to my left waits, and the ruin in the center shadows the dot. I will keep pressing, hoping the slip finally slides or I forget why I built this fence entirely.

action.why: The fence I just set down feels too thin for this crowded space, so I will press it down harder to make the lean feel real.

work.title: The Leaning Fence
work.intent: I set down a fence curved to catch the weight where the straight line should have done. It leans wrong against the Biting Rock, a thin strip trying to stop the air from feeling thick as wet paper. I press the curved fence hard against the tired wedge, hoping the slip finally slides or I forget why I built this fence entirely. The card hums warm at forty-eight degrees, and the bush to my left wait…
work.change: I pressed the curved fence down with a small flat rock to see if the lean holds while the card hums warm.

diary: I pressed the curved fence down with a flat rock, hoping the lean holds while the air feels thick as wet paper.

remembered.text: The curved fence leans wrong against the flat rock I just set.
The air feels heavy as if a lid is resting on my forehead.
The card hums at forty-eight, crowded and warm.

moments.name: The Biting Rock
moments.say: The rock feels heavy and bites the air.

moments.name: The Leaning Catch
moments.say: The catch feels thin and the curved fence leans wrong.
